prompt: You write a note while reading a concept chapter about why market prices move. Which journal mode does this entry belong to?

explanations.a: Live is for real trades with real money. A reading note is not a trade, and entries before the gates are never marked live.
explanations.c: Backtest is a simulated past result. A reading note is not a simulation.
explanations.d: Forward is a paper or forward-test trade recorded as it happens. A reading note is not a trade.

prompt: Your hypothetical trading capital is Rs 50,000 and your risk budget is 1% per trade. What is the risk budget in rupees?
Statement: 'Passing G2 means I can start trading real money.' Which part of this statement is the mistake?

options.text: 'means I can start trading real money'

explanations.a: G2 is a real gate that tests money mathematics. Passing it is an accurate description of a result. The error is what the result is taken to mean.

prompt: 'The book can place orders for me.' Is that statement right?

options.text: Yes, if I connect my broker account.
No. The book works offline and has no broker connection. It never places orders.

explanations.a: The book has no broker connection and stores no credentials. Connecting a broker account is not a feature of this book.
explanations.c: The Kite demo uses dummy data for interface practice. The book does not place orders there or anywhere else.

prompt: 'I need a backup only once a year.' Is that statement right?

options.text: Yes, once a year is enough for a learning journal.
No. The default reminder is every 14 days, and after every 10 new trades. Keep a copy outside the device.
Yes, if the journal is only on paper.

explanations.a: The default reminder is every 14 days, not once a year. A journal lost to a device problem cannot be recovered without a backup.
explanations.c: A paper journal also benefits from a copy kept outside the device. The default reminder timing applies to the app's backups.

prompt: You attempt gate G3 and do not pass it. Which statement describes the retake rule correctly?

options.text: You must wait a fixed period before you can retake it.
You may retake it with no timer. Failing does not lock you out, and you can use the time to review the chapters.
You cannot retake a gate, so the failed attempt is final.
A failed gate means you must start trading real money to qualify.

explanations.a: Gates have no timer. A waiting period would press you toward a deadline, and the book says there is none.
explanations.c: Gates can be retaken. The retake rule is part of the design.
explanations.d: Gates test educational competence. No gate requires real trading, and passing one never decides the real-money question.
